messages:
adele: Heads-up: svcwatch alerted that inference headless svc 'model-serving' lost endpoints on several edge-us-west nodes after the GPU scale-down at ~02:04 UTC. Clients hit 503s when traffic was routed to those nodes.

samir: Which svc type? headless or ClusterIP?

adele: headless (cluster uses headless for POD affinity + custom sidecar routing). We rely on EndpointSlices for local node routing + ipvs.

lina: saw a short spike in kube-proxy restarts around the same time on the drained nodes. Could be conntrack entries outliving endpoints.

noah: Any kube-controller-manager errors? EndpointSlice controller owns slice creation.

adele: logs from svcwatch and kube-controller-manager attached below. svcwatch shows it dropped endpoints, but kubernetes didn't recreate EndpointSlices for 3m.

ops-bot: [alert] svcwatch: model-serving endpoints decreased from 120 -> 0 on node gpu-edge-07 (pod eviction)

adele: kubectl get endpointslices -n inference --selector=kubernetes.io/service-name=model-serving
```
NAME                                        ADDRESS-TYPE   ENDPOINTS   PORTS
model-serving-xx-0                          IPv4           0           8080/TCP
model-serving-xx-1                          IPv4           40          8080/TCP
model-serving-xx-2                          IPv4           80          8080/TCP
```
Notice slice 0 is empty and corresponds to gpu-edge-07 range.

samir: run: kubectl describe endpointslice model-serving-xx-0 -n inference and kubectl get endpoints -o yaml. Maybe topology hints/conditional evicting.

adele: describe shows lastChangeTrigger: NodeDrainEvent and controller annotation: controller.kubernetes.io/paused: "false". But controller logs show throttling: "rate limit exceeded" when reconciling EndpointSlices for that service.

noah: That rate limit is weird — we didn't change QPS. Could scale-down burst + heavy webhook calls cause short-term leader churn? Check controller leader election logs.

lina: also check kube-proxy mode: ipvs vs iptables. ipvs on these nodes; ipvs rules may not be updated when slices disappear -> stale VIP -> traffic drops. Run `ipvsadm -Ln` and `conntrack -L | grep <pod-ip>` on gpu-edge-07.

maria: I pulled ipvs on node: 
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.96.123.8:8080 rr
  -> 10.2.17.33:8080              Masq    1      0          12
  -> 10.2.40.11:8080              Masq    1      0          0
```
We had entries pointing to drained pod IPs. conntrack shows ESTABLISHED entries for client flows that now map to removed pods.

samir: So two things: EndpointSlice update delay + conntrack/IPVS stale entries. For ephemeral model-serving traffic it's killing requests when a conntrack mapping hits an evicted pod. Need a draining hook to flush conntrack or trigger ipvs sync.

adele: Proposed mitigations: 1) patch node drain hook to run `conntrack -D --orig-dst <pod-ip>` for pods in model-serving, 2) bump EndpointSlice controller burst QPS for control plane, 3) add a short pre-evict readiness-probe delay so svcwatch can migrate. Thoughts?

noah: 1 is doable but we should avoid deleting too many conntrack entries globally. Limit to pod IPs. 2 is risky on control plane suddenly handling bursts but ok as temporary rollout. 3 is good for safety.

lina: Also consider using externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster for the LB that fronts edge nodes — it avoids relying on NodeLocal routing in some edge cases, but might increase egress cost.

maria: Logged a small runbook for manual mitigation when this happens: drain --> run conntrack flush for drained pod IPs --> verify EndpointSlice reappear -> ipvs sync (sudo systemctl restart kube-proxy) if needed.

samir: Can you add runbook steps + a short automation PR to run the conntrack deletion in the drain hook for services labeled `inference.redwood.io/flush-conntrack=true`? Keep it opt-in for now.

adele: Will do. Opening issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3321 (in the thread). Planning a canary patch to node-drain hook + controller QPS bump tomorrow during low traffic window.

ops-bot: [incident-note] INFRA-3321 created by adele at 1934568000

noah: One more ask: add monitoring to alert if EndpointSlice count for a service drops >50% for >30s and EndpointSlice controller is returning 429/5xx. That will catch this earlier.

adele: Added to INFRA-3321 checklist. Thanks all :thumbsup:
